Assessment incorporating SLOOS: The FOMC statement emphasizes continued accommodation alongside a measured taper, consistent with a constructive outlook but tempered by inflation and pandemic-related risks. The latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to broadly accommodative bank lending conditions that modestly reinforce the near-term growth and credit flow implied by the statement: banks eased standards across residential real estate, multifamily, nonfarm nonresidential (CRE), and consumer credit (including credit cards and autos), raised credit limits on cards, and reduced auto loan rates; foreign banks reported stronger CRE demand and eased CRE standards. While some categories showed weaker current demand (notably C&I and auto), banks expect stronger demand ahead for C&I and credit cards. This mix suggests credit supply is supportive and expected loan demand is improving, incrementally lifting the near-term tone. That said, the easing in standards and strong risk appetite also echo the Financial Stability Report’s caution on elevated valuations and nonbank vulnerabilities, arguing for vigilance as taper proceeds.

Overall tone: constructive with a slight positive tilt from SLOOS, but still cautious given elevated vulnerabilities flagged in the FSR.

Key sentence: “In light of the substantial further progress the economy has made toward the Committee’s goals since last December, the Committee decided to begin reducing the monthly pace of its net asset purchases.”
